title: Conditioning under a product law
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of its summary $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$. Suppose the conditional law of the special-bit pair on the fiber $Z=z$ is the product of the conditional laws of Alice's and Bob's special bits. For any Boolean value $b_Y$ such that the fiber measure of the event that Bob's special bit equals $b_Y$ is nonzero, the conditional law of Alice's special bit on the fiber equals the pushforward under Alice's special-bit map of the fiber measure further conditioned on that event.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic length-$n$ disjointness protocol
the conditional special-pair law equals the product of the conditional marginal laws

replaced:
Fix a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$ and an achievable
value $z$ of the record $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$, and write $\mu_z$ for the hard
distribution conditioned on the fiber $Z=z$. Let $X_T$ and $Y_T$ denote Alice's and
Bob's bits at the special coordinate $T$, and suppose that under $\mu_z$ the pair
$(X_T,Y_T)$ has product law, i.e. the law of $(X_T,Y_T)$ equals the product of the law
of $X_T$ and the law of $Y_T$. Then for every $b_Y\in\{\text{false},\text{true}\}$ such
that the event $\{Y_T=b_Y\}$ has positive $\mu_z$-mass, the law of $X_T$ under $\mu_z$
coincides with the law of $X_T$ under $\mu_z$ conditioned further on $\{Y_T=b_Y\}$.
